tagline: A long horseshoe from tie hack country to mountain man country.
intro: From Dubois on the upper Wind River, the byway climbs over the Continental Divide at Togwotee Pass under the ash- and lava-banded cliffs of the Absarokas. At Moran Junction it turns south through Grand Teton National Park, where the range rises 7,000 feet above the valley floor with no foothills in the way, and on to Jackson. Then it follows Hoback Canyon past Bondurant to Pinedale.
Dubois was once headquarters for cow outfits and tie hack crews. Pinedale, at the far end, lies in the old country of the fur trappers' rendezvous.

moments.title: Tie Hack Memorial
moments.text: The memorial remembers the men who cut lodgepole above the Wind River, sawed it by hand into railroad ties eight feet long and floated them downriver, until the work was mechanized in the 1940s.

moments.title: Togwotee Pass
moments.text: The pass carries the name of Togwotee, who led the Jones Expedition over it in 1873, and winter snowfall up here often tops 25 feet.

moments.title: Upper Green River Rendezvous Site
moments.text: South of the highway, where Horse Creek meets the Green, at least five of the fur trade rendezvous of 1825 to 1840 were held, and the ground keeps no evidence of any of them.

practical: The whole route is open year-round, though blizzards can shut the road over Togwotee Pass for days at a time.
